why: This round ran after READY was accepted and after retro removed .legion/INFRA-839/, which is why previousHandoff is empty: the directory this file sits in was deleted by retro's own last commit and is written here afresh. INFRA-514's architect ordered the round because this pull request's own risk list had named the hole: once sjawhar/legion#2395 merged, Dispatch's outbox would send a role route to an unheld role nowhere at all, recording the route reached and sending nothing, and acceptance item 1 of this issue - a Dispatch role-routed event to an unheld role reaches the role's next holder once - would have been false on its first day. #2395 merged at 02:29:19Z as squash 70d73cce0. The architect ruled the move lands with this change rather than after it, so the head moved past the accepted READY deliberately and the issue returned to implementing.

answersReviewFindings.finding: The move itself: after #2395, forwardOf records an unheld role's route as reached and sends nothing, so the kept lane never sees a Dispatch role event to an unheld role.
answersReviewFindings.fix: forwardOf's two keepable skips - roles.Unclaimed, and roles.Lapsed whose claim the release dropped or found missing, the same two states as the listener's own roleKeepable - now keep through keptOrSkipped, which publishes to bus.KeptRoleSubject(role) under bus.KeptMsgID(dedupeKey, role), the call the listener's keep makes. roles.Valid is carried across, so a role token no claim can name is still skipped. The third lapsed case, a claim the restart grace retained, stays the error #2395 made it. No change to #2395's production code and no grant change: Dispatch's user already publishes notifications.> through listenerGrant, and the keep rides #2395's own send path, so exactly-once is the stream's dedupe on the Nats-Msg-Id and order is #2395's.
answersReviewFindings.test: TestARoleRouteToAnUnheldRoleIsKeptForTheRolesNextHolder, TestAKeptRoleRouteRetriedAfterALostAcknowledgementIsKeptOnce, TestAKeptRoleRouteWhoseKeepFailedStaysPendingAndIsKeptOnTheRetry, TestARoleRouteWhoseClaimTheGraceRetainedErrsWithNothingKept, TestARoleTokenNoClaimCanNameIsSkippedWithNothingKept and TestAKeptRoleRouteIsPublishedOnTheRolesKeptLaneUnderTheKeptMsgID in internal/dispatch/outbox/role_keep_test.go, and the end-to-end TestAnEventDispatchRoutedToAnUnheldRoleReachesTheRolesNextHolder in cmd/listener/dispatch_kept_role_test.go. The second and third are the two the architect named beyond the first.

answersReviewFindings.finding: Deliberate change 1 to #2395's own tests: window_test.go's four order assertions encode that an unheld role contributes nothing to the stream, which is exactly the behaviour this round changes. Their fixture routes every seeded event to role:reviewer, which no session claims, so the totals read 500 where they want 300.
answersReviewFindings.fix: The expectation is split rather than raised, on the architect's condition that the tests keep testing order: assertStreamInOrderPerDestination keeps its old numbers and its ordering rule but skips subjects under bus.KeptRoleSubjectPrefix, and a new assertKeptLaneInOrder asserts the kept copies separately, one per role-routed event, each under its KeptMsgID, each issue's in event id order. So a lost or reordered ordinary message still fails and a missing kept copy fails too. Derived per test from its fixture: wantOnDestinations = count + count/2, wantKept = count.
answersReviewFindings.test: The four assertions themselves, in TestABacklogPublishedAcrossANATSOutageKeepsItsOrder, TestABatchCutOffInFlightKeepsItsOrder and TestAnOutboxThatDiesBetweenAckAndMarkPublishesAgainWithoutDuplicates. One finding while doing it, written into the helper: the kept lane is one destination shared by every issue and the outbox's per-destination chains interleave across issues, so global id order does not hold there - each issue's copies are in order, which is what the helper asserts.

answersReviewFindings.finding: Deliberate change 2: cmd/listener/delivery_role_stale_holder_test.go, a test #2395 added, asserts that a holder which stopped heartbeating gets its claim released and a delivery_failed exception. This issue's approved Outcome answers that case the other way - a message published while its holder's session is stopped is kept for the next holder - so the two changes collide on one case.
answersReviewFindings.fix: Escalated to INFRA-514's architect rather than decided, with both texts quoted. The architect ruled the approved outcome stands, and that keeping serves #2395's own stated reason better than refusing: the claim is still released and the copy waits for a live holder rather than being dropped into a probably-dead session. The stale-holder row now expects no exception, the claim still released, and exactly one copy on the kept lane under its KeptMsgID. The fresh-holder row is untouched, since the freshness test is still what separates the two.
answersReviewFindings.test: TestCoreRoleDeliverySkipsAHolderThatStoppedHeartbeating's stale-holder row, which failed deterministically on the stacked head before the change with 'exception reason "", claim now held by ""; want reason "delivery_failed" and the claim released'.

answersReviewFindings.finding: Deliberate change 3, the architect's addition: the sender that keeps its own queue must still get the refusal it had for a stale holder.
answersReviewFindings.fix: A third row in that test: keep: false through POST /v1/messages/publish still releases the claim, keeps nothing, and refuses the sender. Its wording departs from the ruling's literal delivery_failed, and the departure is stated rather than hidden: keep is the publish route's request field alone, since round 4 deleted Envelope.Keep, so a raw role publish has no field to carry the opt-out and the lane always keeps; and that route answers its sender rather than publishing an exception, so the refusal is 404 with reason holder_lapsed, holder and claim_released true. The listener's record line for it reads delivery_status failed, reason holder_lapsed. The architect was told the correction before it went in.
answersReviewFindings.test: The new row, 'a stale holder whose sender keeps its own queue: keep false is refused 404 and keeps nothing'.

trickyParts: My pod was replaced mid-work at 00:45-01:39Z and took the unpushed merge and move with it. The INFRA merge lane had rescued it as legion/INFRA-839-rescue-jj-172ee713702d, a conflict-free merge of 04287268 with 1ccdd0e7 carrying the whole move, so it was taken back whole rather than rebuilt. That is the third pod replacement of this issue and the second rescue taken.

Because the branch had already merged #2395 unsquashed, main's squash made the same content arrive twice: 12 of the second merge's 13 files resolve as this branch's text whole. That is a fact about this merge and not a rule - each was still proven per file by line sets, which is what this branch's own LEGION-668 learning now prescribes.

The kept lane is one destination shared by every issue, and the outbox's per-destination chains interleave across issues, so global event-id order does not hold on that lane. assertKeptLaneInOrder asserts each issue's copies in order instead, which is the rule throughput_test.go already documents for a live holder's agent subject.

#2395's multiprocess suite needs more than CI's 20-minute timeout in this pod: the first attempt ended 'panic: test timed out after 20m0s' with no --- FAIL after 163 tests, and the same suite passed in 1653 s at 3300 s.
